name: Grid
summary: Equal columns for things compared side by side (options, variants), as many as fit at `size.column-min` each, a gutter apart; rows sit a group's space apart. Below two columns' width it becomes one column, so it never scrolls sideways from 320 px. With `ratio` it draws two uneven columns instead (a wide and a narrow one, or a heading beside its content) that stack when their container is narrow. Not for a page's regions (use LibraryLayout), a column of unrelated content (use Stack) or a wrapping row of small marks (use Cluster).
a11y: A plain `div` with no role: it arranges, it doesn't group for assistive technology. Reading order is the source order, row by row.

props.name: children
props.description: The things to compare, in reading order; each takes one column.

props.name: max
props.description: The most columns, even with room for more: 2 keeps four things 2 × 2 instead of 3 + 1. Default: as many as fit. Ignored with `ratio`.

props.name: ratio
props.description: Two uneven columns instead of equal ones (IP20): `2:1` and `3:2` give the start column the larger share, `1:2` and `2:3` the end column; `aside` keeps the start column at `--c-grid-aside` (a heading beside its content) and gives the end column the rest. Children alternate start, end, start, end. Below two columns' width (two `size.column-min` and a gutter) they stack in source order. Default: equal columns.

settings.description: The start column's width when ratio is aside, a heading beside its content (default size.column-min, 16rem).
